primary_claim: An LLM-based audit using Claude Opus 4.5 to rate test coverage found genuine issues in roughly 13 of Terminal-Bench 2.0's 89 tasks despite the benchmark's extensive human review, including a task where target files were already visible in the container (enabling a shortcut that would pass the tests) and a task whose oracle solution itself violates the stated task instructions.

effect.metric: count of tasks flagged with genuine test-coverage issues out of 89 audited
effect.value: Claude rated 14 tasks a 3 and 1 task a 2 (out of 89); manual review confirmed 2 of these 15 were false positives, leaving roughly 13 tasks with genuine issues

contradicts_or_qualifies: Qualifies Terminal-Bench 2's claim of being thoroughly human- and LM-verified ('some of the highest quality environments they have seen') by finding tasks with reward-hackable shortcuts and an oracle solution that violates its own instructions

Also cites that LiveCodeBench Pro's public test set differs from the rigorously-vetted Codeforces test cases it claims to use, allowing some incorrect solutions to pass, and that FutureHouse found about 30% of Humanity's Last Exam chemistry/biology answers are likely wrong
stated_future_work: Scale AI-audit infrastructure like Fulcrum's Lunette to more benchmarks
Adopt fine-grained version control so benchmarks can release quick patch versions (e.g. Terminal-Bench 2.1) that fix found issues without changing the task set
Require sample data submission and direct data auditing by peer reviewers when benchmark papers are submitted to conferences
Increase community/financial support for ongoing benchmark maintenance
limitations_stated: Three flagged tasks were not reviewed because the author felt he lacked the relevant expertise to vet them
Claude's audit produced false positives, incorrectly rating two tasks a 3 that the author judged to have sufficient test coverage
One task's audit prompt was entirely blocked by content moderation (flagged for discussing 'stealing' neural network weights), preventing the model from ever engaging with that task
Claude Opus 4.5 had not yet been released when Terminal-Bench 2 was created, so its authors could not have used it themselves during their own verification
quote: Claude rated fourteen tasks a 3 and one task a 2.
